# sca config

[← Command reference](../commands.md)

`<sca_options>` are the [global options](../commands.md#global-options).

```text
The configuration command help

The configuration command is used for managing the sca configuration.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] config [<config_options>] <config_command>

config_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

allowed values for the config_command are:

  - get             - to retrieve current configuration information
  - set             - to change current configuration information
  - create          - to initially generate the configuration
  - resolve         - to resolve configuration derived settings from the base
                    settings
  - load            - to load configuration from a file
  - save            - to save configuration to a file
  - reset           - reset configuration to defaults
```

**See also**

```text
Run 'sca config <config_command> -h' for getting help specific to a the given
config_command.
```

### Configuration Keys

| Key | Description | Example |
|-----|-------------|---------|
| `ca` | CA name (organization) | `mycompany` |
| `subca` | Sub-CA name (administrator) | `admin` |
| `service` | Current service name | `gitlab` |
| `host` | Current host name | `server1` |
| `user` | Current user name | `john` |
| `domain` | Domain suffix | `.mycompany.com` |

**Additional keys:**

| Key | Description | Default |
|-----|-------------|---------|
| `ca_bits` | CA key size | `4096` |
| `subca_bits` | Sub-CA key size | `4096` |
| `service_bits` | Service key size | `2048` |
| `host_bits` | Host key size | `2048` |
| `user_bits` | User key size | `2048` |

See the [Configuration Reference](../configuration.md) for the configuration files.

**Subcommands**

- [create](#sca-config-create) - to initially generate the configuration
- [get](#sca-config-get) - to retrieve current configuration information
- [load](#sca-config-load) - to load configuration from a file
- [reset](#sca-config-reset) - reset configuration to defaults
- [resolve](#sca-config-resolve) - to resolve configuration derived settings from the base settings
- [save](#sca-config-save) - to save configuration to a file
- [set](#sca-config-set) - to change current configuration information

## sca config create

```text
The configuration create command help

The configuration create command is used for creating the initial sca
configuration.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] config [<config_options>] create [<create_options>] <entity>

config_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

create_options:

  -h, --help              - print this help
  -r, --recreate          - recreate any existing files by backing them up and
                            recreating from default

allowed values for the entity are:

  - ca            - openssl.config generation for current certificate authority
  - subca         - openssl.config generation for current sub-ordinate certificate authority
  - user          - openssl.config generation for current user
  - host          - openssl.config generation for current host
  - service       - openssl.config generation for current service
  - all           - for creation of all of the configuration files
```

Generates the initial configuration files in `~/.sca/config/`.

## sca config get

```text
The configuration get command help

The configuration get command is used for retrieving the sca configuration.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] config [<config_options>] get [<get_options>] <entity> <entity_id>

config_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

get_options:

  -h, --help              - print this help

allowed values for the entity are:

  - ca            - for current certificate authority
  - subca         - for current sub-ordinate certificate authority
  - user          - for current user
  - host          - for current host
  - service       - for current service

entity_id stands for the id of the

the reported entity info depend on the entity requested:

for entity ca entity info is as follows:

  <name> <caps_name>

for entity subca entity info is as follows:

  <subca> <subca_name> <subca first name> <subca last name> <subca given name> <subca initials>

for entity user entity info is as follows:

  <user> <user_name> <user_first_name> <user_last_name> <user_given_name> <user_initials>

for entity host entity info is as follows:

  <host_name>

for entity service entity info is as follows:

  <service_name>
```

**Examples:**

```bash
# Get all configuration
sca config get

# Get specific value
sca config get ca
sca config get domain
```

## sca config load

```text
The configuration load command help

The configuration load command is used for loading the sca configuration from a
file.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] config [<config_options>] load [<load_options>] <sca_config_file>

config_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

load_options:

  -h, --help              - print this help

The sca_config_file should be an existing file containing the sca configuration.
It is a plain bash script file exporting default variables settings.
```

**Example:**

```bash
# Load configuration from file
sca config load ~/my-sca-config.sh
```

## sca config reset

```text
The configuration reset command help

The configuration reset command is used for resetting the current sca
configuration to their default values. it is useful only in context of sca
itself or in dot sourcing scenario as it doesn't affect the parent execution
environment.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] config [<config_options>] reset [<reset_options>]

config_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

reset_options:

  -h, --help              - print this help
```

```bash
sca config reset
```

---

## sca config resolve

```text
The configuration resolve command help

The configuration resolve command is used for resolving the derived settings
of sca configuration. It is used only in dot sourced loading scenario or within
sca code itself.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] config [<config_options>] resolve [<resolve_options>]

config_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

resolve_options:

  -h, --help              - print this help
```

Resolves derived settings (file paths, full names) from the base configuration. Used internally and in scripted scenarios.

```bash
sca config resolve
```

## sca config save

```text
The configuration save command help

The configuration save command is used for saving the current sca configuration
to a file.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] config [<config_options>] save [<save_options>] <sca_config_file>

config_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

save_options:

  -h, --help              - print this help

The sca_config_file will be created with the sca configuration. The file format
is plain bash script exporting default variables settings.
```

**Example:**

```bash
# Save current configuration
sca config save ~/my-sca-config.sh
```

The configuration file format is a bash script with exported variables.

## sca config set

```text
The configuration set command help

The configuration set command is used for setting the sca configuration.
```

**Syntax**

```text
sca [<sca_options>] config [<config_options>] set [<set_options>] <entity> <entity_id> <entity_info>

config_options:

  -h, --help      - print this help

set_options:

  -h, --help              - print this help

allowed values for the entity are:

  - ca            - for current certificate authority
  - subca         - for current sub-ordinate certificate authority
  - user          - for current user
  - host          - for current host
  - service       - for current service

entity_id stands for the id of the

the required entity_info depend on the entity requested:

for entity ca entity info is as follows:

  <name> <caps_name>

for entity subca entity info is as follows:

  <subca> <subca_name> <subca first name> <subca last name> <subca given name> <subca initials>

for entity user entity info is as follows:

  <user> <user_name> <user first name> <user last name> <user given name> <user initials>

for entity host entity info is as follows:

  <host name>

for entity service entity info is as follows:

  <service name>
```

**Examples:**

```bash
# Set CA name
sca config set ca mycompany

# Set domain
sca config set domain .mycompany.com

# Set current service
sca config set service webapp
```
